parts.subtitle: What Ignition is, how to sign in and get around, and what your role can see.

chapters.title: Welcome to Ignition
chapters.html:
Ignition is the influencer-marketing CRM for Legend of Toys. It tracks the creators we work with and every deal we run with them, from first contact through the live post and its results. This manual is your self-serve guide to every screen in it.

The two things Ignition tracks

Influencers

The people and channels we work with: their reach, contact details, quality rating, and which list they sit on (the proven roster, the parked B-List, or archived).

Engagements

A single deal with one influencer (also called a “deal”). Each engagement moves through a pipeline of stages and records the terms, costs, logistics and performance.

How a deal flows

Every engagement moves along a pipeline. The happy path runs: Proposed → Planning → Shipped → Delivered → Draft received → Scheduled → Live. Live is the finish line for a video deal — the video is up, the deal is done. A deal that does not work out exits to Ghosted, Dropped or Cancelled, and On hold and Delayed are there for a deal that has stalled without dying.

ⓘ Dropped costs money. Cancelled does not.

The difference matters, because it decides whether the deal shows up in your spend. Dropped is a loss: the goods went out and never became a video, so its cost keeps counting in Reports, monthly spend and CPM. Cancelled is for a deal called off before anything was spent — postponed, or stopped before the products shipped. A cancelled deal keeps its record but is left out of every total, and it will never be chased as overdue to post.

You can move a deal to any stage, in any order — real deals do not queue politely — with one exception: a deal starts in Proposed and cannot move on until it is approved. Approving it sends it straight to Planning, so you never have to approve and then advance it as two separate jobs. You can still drop or ghost a proposal you are turning down without approving it first.

ⓘ Two badges, two meanings

Watch for two colour systems. A stage badge shows where a deal is in the pipeline (orange means it is Live or being Tracked, the “money on air” stages). A rating badge (Green, Yellow, Red, Unrated) is your quality judgment of an influencer, not a deal. Do not confuse them.

How to use this manual

Each chapter covers one screen: what it is for, how to read it, and what to do. Jump to the screen you are on using the Contents page or your PDF reader’s bookmarks. Chapters are tagged with the roles that use them:

Marketer   Lead   Admin

⚠ Some screens are still being built

Ignition is live but a few screens are deliberately partial today (marked “Phase B” in the app): Reports, Campaigns and parts of Discount Codes show data but do not yet have full create/edit tools. Each chapter says clearly what works now.

chapters.title: Signing In & Getting Around
chapters.html:
Ignition opens with your work Google account and everything sits in one sidebar. This chapter covers signing in and finding your way around.

Signing in

Open ignition.legendoftoys.com and sign in with your @legendoftoys.com Google account. Personal accounts are refused; if sign-in loops, sign out of any personal Google account first or use a fresh browser profile.

The menu

GroupWhat lives here
WORKDashboard, Influencers, Engagements, New Deal.
LISTSRoster, B-List, UGC, Campaigns, Codes.
ANALYZEReports (for leads and admins).
ADMINUsers and Import (admins only).

You only see the groups your role allows. Most list screens have a search box, and amounts are shown in rupees (₹).

ⓘ Screens load once

Ignition screens load their data when you open them and do not refresh on their own. To see new information after something changes, change a filter or reopen the page. Most lists show up to 100 or 200 rows; if a list looks cut off, narrow it with the search box or filters.

chapters.title: Roles & What You Can See
chapters.html:
Ignition gives each person the access that matches their job. This chapter explains the three roles used throughout this manual.

The three roles

Marketer

Marketing Team. Runs deals day to day: searches influencers, opens engagements, advances them through the pipeline, sets quality ratings and adds notes.

Lead

Lead. Everything a marketer does, plus access to the Reports. Leads do not approve deals — final approval sits with the Marketing head (admin) since 26 Aug 2026.

Admin

Admin. Full access, including the admin screens (the user-roles reference and the data-import runbook).

ⓘ How access actually works

Ignition uses the shared company permission map. The relevant permissions are ignition_view, ignition_manage, ignition_approve, ignition_reports_view and ignition_admin, bundled into the ignition_manager and ignition_lead roles (admins get everything). ignition_approve is admin-only: it is what lets someone sign off a proposed deal, and everyone else keeps ignition_manage, so they can still create deals and move them along. Roles are actually assigned in Garage (the store app) at its Users screen, not inside Ignition. If you cannot reach something you should, ask an admin to set your role there.

Who sees what

AreaMarketerLeadAdmin
Dashboard, Influencers, Engagements, Lists•••
Create & advance deals, set ratings•••
Reports••
Approving a proposed deal•
User Roles, Sheet Import•

parts.subtitle: The dashboard, the influencer roster, the deal pipeline, and working a single engagement.

chapters.title: Dashboard
chapters.html:
The Dashboard is Ignition’s overview: a quick count of engagements by health. It is the landing screen when you sign in.

What it’s for
Engagements by health, at a glance.
Read or act?
Read-only.
Who
Marketer Lead Admin
Shows
Four count cards.

The four cards

CardMeaning
ActiveEngagements currently in progress.
LiveEngagements live right now (orange, the “on air” deals).
ClosedEngagements finished and closed.
GhostedDeals where the influencer went silent (red).
ⓘ Counts only, for now

The Dashboard shows these four numbers and nothing more: no charts or trends yet. For the detail behind them, open Engagements and filter by stage.

chapters.title: Influencers
chapters.html:
Influencers is the searchable roster of every creator and channel we know. From here you open a creator’s profile, see their deal history, and set the quality rating that guides whether we work with them again.

What it’s for
Browsing creators and rating them.
Read or act?
Read; set the quality rating.
Who
Marketer Lead Admin
Lists
Master · B-List · Archived.

Profiles with no usable link

A strip at the top of the list counts influencers whose channel link is not a real web address — usually a browser tab title pasted by mistake, like “(9) Instagram”. These break profile matching and can make one person look like several. Click fix these to work through them.

Where the handle is clear, a suggested link is offered and one click accepts it. Where it is not — a display name rather than a handle, or a YouTube channel — there is a box to paste the real profile URL.

⚠ Check the suggestion before accepting it

A suggestion is built from the handle, so it can point at somebody else entirely if the handle is a common word. It is never applied on its own; that click is you confirming it is the right person.

The list

Tabs split influencers into Master, B-List and Archived. Each row shows the code, channel (and person), type (nano, micro, macro, brand, store), category, reach, location, and a rating badge. Search by code, handle, name, phone or email, and filter by type and rating. Click a row to open the profile.

Location

When you add or edit a creator, Location offers a list of cities and states as you type. Pick one where you can — typing the same city three different ways is what left Bengaluru sitting in the filter four times over, each version finding a quarter of the people. If the creator’s town is not on the list, type it anyway: the field accepts anything, and a known spelling is tidied up for you when you move on (BLR becomes Bangalore, Kerela becomes Kerala).

The profile, and the rating

A creator’s detail page shows their identity and contact details, and a table of all their engagements. Its key action is the quality rating: four buttons in the header set the creator to Green, Yellow, Red or Unrated. This is the team’s signal on whether a creator is worth working with again, and it drives the rating filter and the Roster.

⚠ Rating saves instantly

Clicking a rating button saves immediately with no confirmation, so a wrong click is live at once: just click the correct one to fix it. “First invite: Not sent” on the profile means no invite has gone out to that creator yet.

chapters.title: Engagements
chapters.html:
Engagements is the deal pipeline: every influencer deal we are running, filterable by stage and type. From here you browse deals and start new ones.

What it’s for
Browsing the deal pipeline.
Read or act?
Read; start a new deal.
Who
Marketer Lead Admin
Tabs
All · Live · Scheduled · Draft rcvd · Delivered.

Reading it

Tabs give quick stage filters (All, Live, Scheduled, Draft rcvd, Delivered). Each row shows the engagement number, the influencer (channel + code), type (Video or UGC), the current stage badge, the deal type, the product and its variant, the expected post date, the actual post date, views, CPM and total cost. Search by engagement number, video link, tracking or order. On the All tab, stage chips let you pick several stages at once; on the other tabs the tab itself sets the stage.

The four tiles

Above the table sit four tiles — Deals, Total cost, Views and Blended CPM. They always describe exactly the rows you are looking at, so filter the list down to a product, a stage or a date range and the tiles re-count for that selection. Blended CPM is worked out across the deals that actually have views; deals that have not posted yet are left out of it, otherwise their cost would make the CPM look worse than it is.

Filtering

Beyond the tabs and stage chips there is a product filter (the products actually on deals, with a count each) and a posting-date filter with four modes:

  • Any date — no date filtering.
  • Upcoming — not posted yet, expected today or later.
  • Overdue — not posted, and the expected date has already passed.
  • Date range — pick a From and To. A deal is judged on its actual post date, or its expected date if it has not posted.
ⓘ Your filters stay put

Filters survive going into a deal and coming back — they only reset when you clear them yourself with clear all filters. And a deal you edit stays where it is in the list: the order is the order deals were added, so nothing jumps to the top while you are reading.

ⓘ “New Deal” makes an engagement

The orange + New Deal button creates a new engagement (deal and engagement are the same thing here). Click any row to open that engagement and work it.

chapters.title: New Deal
chapters.html:
New Deal creates an engagement: pick the influencer and enter the deal terms. The new deal starts at the beginning of the pipeline, ready for you to advance.

What it’s for
Starting a new influencer deal.
Read or act?
Action: creates an engagement.
Who
Marketer Lead Admin
Required
An influencer.

Picking the product

Start typing in the Product box and pick from the list. Picking fills in both boxes — the product name in Product, the model and colour in Variant / colour — and pulls in the cost, so Goodies fills itself where we know what the item costs us. The selling price shows underneath with a use button, so you never have to go and look it up.

ⓘ Pick it rather than typing it

Typing a product name freehand still works, but a typed name is only text: no cost, no price, and it cannot point the tracking link at the right product page. Picking from the list is what connects the deal to the real product.

⚠ The wooden kits have no cost on record

Goodies will not fill itself for the Harry Potter crests or the other L.O.T Build items — we hold costs for only a few of them — so type the figure in. The selling price is still shown underneath to save you looking.

Creating a deal

  1. Find the influencer. Search by code, handle or name (type at least two characters) and pick from the results. Use Change to reselect.
  2. Set the deal terms. Engagement type (Video or UGC), deal type (Paid, Barter, Affiliate, Paid + Affiliate), payment terms and amount, the product code and variant, and where the deal drives traffic (Website, Amazon, Flipkart).
  3. Create Engagement. The deal is created at stage Identified and opens on its detail page.
ⓘ Only the influencer is required

You can create a deal with a ₹0 amount and a blank product and fill them in later; the only thing you must pick is the influencer. The search shows nothing until you have typed two characters, which is normal. Every new deal begins at the start of the pipeline and is advanced step by step afterwards.

chapters.title: Working an Engagement
chapters.html:
The engagement detail screen is the control centre for one deal: its terms, product, costs, logistics and performance, plus the controls to advance the pipeline, add notes, and flag damage to customer support. This is where most of the work happens.

What it’s for
Running one deal end to end.
Read or act?
The main action screen.
Who
Marketer Lead Admin
Pipeline
7 on the happy path, 3 exits, 2 holds.

The layout

The header shows the engagement number, the influencer, the current stage and deal badges, and two buttons: Advance and Flag Damage to Pitstop. A pipeline stepper shows progress. Below sit cards for Deal Terms, Product, Influencer, Payments, Costs (with the rolled-up total in orange), Logistics, Post-live and Performance (views, orders, ROAS), followed by Notes and a History log.

Deal Terms also records ad rights: whether the creator has agreed we may run the video as a paid ad, what we paid for that specifically, and how long we may run it. The amount is separate from the creator’s fee and counts toward the deal’s total cost. Ad rights shows a dash until someone answers the question — a dash means nobody has recorded it, which is not the same as No.

The Influencer card repeats who the deal is with — handle, name, phone, email, location, platform, type and follower count — so you can check you are looking at the right person without opening their profile. It is read-only; edit the creator on their own page.

The Payments card shows what has been paid against this deal and what is still owed, and every payment carries its screenshot: click it to open the proof. + Record logs a new payment with the creator and deal already filled in. The separate Payments page is still there for spend across all deals.

The tracking link

Every deal can carry its own tracking link — a short lottoys.in address that sends the customer to Legend of Toys and records that the visit came from this creator and this deal. It appears in the Post-live card, in full, with a copy button, because the whole point is to hand the string to a creator.

A deal gets one automatically when it reaches Shipped. For older deals, or if one is missing, click Create tracking link. The link points at the product page whenever we can work out which product the deal is for, and at the shop otherwise. Picking the product from the dropdown when you create the deal is what makes that certain; if it was typed by hand we still match it to the catalogue where the name is unambiguous. Where two different products could be meant, the link deliberately goes to the shop rather than risk sending a creator’s followers to the wrong page.

⚠ Give the creator this link, not the shop address

A plain link to the website cannot be told apart from anyone else’s traffic. Only the tracking link credits the visits, and any resulting orders, to the creator who sent them. Once a creator has posted it, it must not be changed — it is already out in the world on their page.

The deal brief

Preview brief (in the header) writes a draft of the collaboration email for this deal: what we are sending, the posting date, the tracking link, the discount code, and what we would like the creator to include. It also warns you up front if the influencer has no email address on record, or the deal has no tracking link, code or expected post date.

ⓘ It is a draft, and nothing sends it

Ignition cannot email creators. The brief is there to be read, argued with and copied out — use Copy brief and send it yourself. The wording is a starting point and is expected to change.

Approving a proposed deal

A deal sitting in Proposed cannot move on until it is approved. Since 26 Aug 2026 that is the Marketing head’s decision alone; everyone else sees “Approval is with Reann” where the button used to be, and keeps every other control. A deal you are turning down can still be dropped or ghosted without approving it first.

Approving now moves the deal for you. Since 27 Aug 2026 a deal you approve goes straight to Planning (a UGC deal goes to Outreach) — you no longer approve it and then advance it as two separate jobs.

Advancing the deal

Click Advance to move the deal to another stage, with an optional note. The happy path is Proposed, Planning, Shipped, Delivered, Draft received, Scheduled, Live, and Live is the finish line — the video is up, the deal is done. A deal that falls through exits to Ghosted, Dropped or Cancelled (use Cancelled when the deal was called off before anything was spent — it keeps the record but stays out of every spend and CPM total); On hold and Delayed hold a deal that has stalled without dying. You may move to any stage in any order — the one thing you cannot do is leave Proposed without an approval.

ⓘ “Agreed” is gone

The old Agreed stage was retired on 27 Aug 2026: approving a deal is now the go-ahead, so the stage was saying the same thing twice. Deals that were sitting on it moved to Planning. Old history entries still read “Agreed” — that is the record of what happened at the time, not an error.

ⓘ You can skip stages — on purpose

Real deals do not queue politely, so Advance lets you move to any stage in any order. If you skip past a stage on the happy path it simply warns you and lets you continue. Terminal stages are not dead ends either: reopening a ghosted or cancelled deal clears its closing date and puts it back in play. Notes you add and every stage move are recorded in the History log.

⛔ Flagging damage opens a real support ticket

Flag Damage to Pitstop opens a genuine ticket in the Pitstop customer-support system, prefilled with this deal’s influencer info, with a disposition (replacement, refund or repair) and a required description. This is a deliberate manual handoff, used when a product sent to an influencer arrives damaged. Only one Pitstop ticket can be opened per engagement; once raised, its number shows in the Logistics card.

chapters.title: Payments
chapters.html:
Payments is the running log of what we have paid influencers, deal by deal. Every advance and final payment goes here, so the totals at the top always show what has gone out today, this week, this month and all time.

What it’s for
Logging influencer payments.
Read or act?
Read the log; record payments.
Who
Marketer Lead Admin
Tied to
Always a specific deal.

The layout

Four spend tiles sit across the top: Today, This Week, This Month and All Time. Each shows the total paid in that window, the number of payments, and how many different influencers they covered. Below them is the log itself: one row per payment, newest first, showing the date paid, the influencer, the deal, the kind, the amount, and any note. The deal in a row links straight to that engagement.

Recording a payment

  1. Open the form. Click Record Payment in the top right.
  2. Find the influencer. Search by code, handle or name (type at least two characters) and pick from the results. Use Change to reselect.
  3. Pick the deal. Choose which of that influencer’s deals the payment is for. If they only have one, it is selected for you. If they have none, the form tells you to create a deal first.
  4. Enter the details. Choose the kind (Advance, Final or Other), the amount, the date paid, and an optional note such as a transfer reference. Then save.

The three kinds

KindUse it for
AdvanceMoney paid up front, before the work is delivered.
FinalThe balance paid once the deal is done.
OtherAnything that is neither an advance nor a final balance.
ⓘ A payment always belongs to a deal

You cannot log a loose payment against an influencer with no deal: pick the engagement it relates to. Payments recorded here also show up on that engagement’s own page, where the Deal Terms card reads “₹X paid of ₹Y agreed”, so the deal always reflects what has actually been sent.

⚠ Removing a payment is instant

The trash icon at the end of a row deletes that payment straight away, with no undo, and the spend tiles drop to match. Only remove a row if it was logged in error; to correct an amount, delete the wrong row and record the right one.

chapters.title: Schedule
chapters.html:
Schedule shows when deals are going live across the month: a calendar of every post that is either already up or expected, so you can see the content pipeline at a glance and spot quiet or crowded weeks.

What it’s for
When deals go live, by month.
Read or act?
Read-only.
Who
Marketer Lead Admin
Views
Calendar · List.

Who is overdue to post

Above the calendar, a strip counts the creators who were sent something 10 or more days ago and still have not posted. Click it to see who, how many days it has been, and whether they have an email address and a tracking link on record. Clicking a row opens that deal.

ⓘ It lists, it does not chase

Nothing is sent automatically — this is the worklist you work by hand. The strip disappears when nobody is overdue.

Moving around

The header carries the month name with arrows either side to step back and forward a month, and a Today button to jump back to the current month. On the right, two toggles switch between the Calendar and the List view of the same month. A counter shows how many posts fall in the month you are looking at.

Posted vs planned

Each deal appears on its go-live date. If the post is already up, that date is its real post date; if it is still upcoming, the date is the expected post date. A small dot tells the two apart:

DotMeaning
Filled (orange)Posted — the video is live, dated by its real post date.
Hollow (outline)Planned — expected, dated by the date the deal is due to go live.

The two views

In the Calendar view, each day cell lists the influencers posting that day; today’s cell is tinted. If a day has more than four, it shows the first few and a “+N more” line. In the List view, the same deals appear as rows with date, deal, influencer, product, stage, whether each is posted or planned, and a link to the video where one exists. In either view, clicking a deal opens its engagement.

ⓘ Only dated deals show here

A deal appears on the Schedule once it has a go-live date, whether expected or actual. Deals that have no date yet simply do not show up until one is set on the engagement. To change when something lands, set its date on the deal itself, not here.

parts.subtitle: The proven roster, parked candidates, UGC pipeline, campaigns and discount codes.

chapters.title: Roster
chapters.html:
The Roster is the proven-influencer list: every creator who has completed at least one engagement. Open it to find vetted creators and check their quality rating before giving them new work.

What it’s for
Finding proven creators.
Read or act?
Read; click through to a profile.
Who
Marketer Lead Admin
Includes
1+ completed engagement.

Using it

Each row shows the influencer code, channel, type, reach, how many engagements they have, and their rating badge. Filter with the chips: All, Green, Yellow, Red, Unrated. Click a row to open the creator’s profile.

ⓘ Proven only

The Roster lists only creators with at least one completed engagement, so brand-new or in-progress-only creators will not appear here (find those under Influencers or B-List). The list shows up to 200 rows.

chapters.title: B-List
chapters.html:
The B-List is the parked-candidates list: creators who are interested but not a current priority, a “maybe later” bench. Open it to revisit prospects you have talked to but are not actively pursuing.

What it’s for
Parked, lower-priority prospects.
Read or act?
Read; click through to a profile.
Who
Marketer Lead Admin
Includes
Influencers on the B-List.

Using it

Each row shows the code, channel, type, reach, and a Comments column noting why the creator is parked. Click a row to open the profile, where you can move them onto the Master list when you are ready to pursue them.

⚠ B-List means “Plan B”, not “banned”

Despite the name, the B-List is a bench of interested-but-not-yet-aligned creators, not a blocklist. It is where you keep leads warm for later, not where you put people you will not work with.

chapters.title: UGC Pipeline
chapters.html:
The UGC Pipeline tracks commission-based user-generated-content deals, where the creator is paid by results. It shows ad spend, commission and return on ad spend (ROAS) alongside each deal’s stage.

What it’s for
Watching UGC deals and their ROAS.
Read or act?
Read; click through to a deal.
Who
Marketer Lead Admin
Shows
UGC engagements only.

Using it

Each row shows the engagement number, influencer, the current stage badge, the product, ad spend, commission, and ROAS (return on ad spend, to two decimals). The list is filtered to UGC deals automatically. Click a row to open the engagement and edit its numbers.

ⓘ “₹0” usually means not entered yet

Ad spend and commission default to ₹0 and ROAS shows a dash until measured, so an empty-looking row usually means the figures have not been entered yet, not that performance was zero. You enter those numbers on the engagement’s detail page, not here. The list shows up to 200 rows.

chapters.title: Campaigns
chapters.html:
Campaigns lists multi-video deal groupings: a single influencer deal that bundles several videos under one campaign number. Open it to see all campaigns and their agreed value at a glance.

What it’s for
Multi-video deal groupings.
Read or act?
Read-only.
Who
Marketer Lead Admin
Status
Phase B (view-only today).

Reading it

Each row shows the campaign number, the influencer, how many videos it bundles, the agreed total (₹) and a status. Click a row to open the campaign, where you get its rolled-up numbers — linked deals, how many have posted, total spend, views and orders — and can attach or detach deals.

The campaign brief

Each campaign has a Campaign brief slot: press Upload brief and pick the file you want the creators to work from. It is stored privately — the link the app opens is short-lived, so the brief is never a public URL — and you can Replace it whenever the brief is rewritten. The name and upload date show next to it, so it is obvious when a campaign is running on an old brief.

chapters.title: Discount Codes
chapters.html:
Discount Codes shows the pre-minted code pool and which codes have been used, on which order, and against which engagement. Open it to check code usage.

What it’s for
Seeing the code pool and usage.
Read or act?
Read-only.
Who
Marketer Lead Admin
Tabs
All · Unused · Used.

Naming an affiliate code

When you issue an affiliate code from a deal you can give it a name of your own — letters and numbers, at least three of them — instead of the generated one. Leave the box empty and a name is generated as before.

⚠ Gift codes are always random, and cannot be named

A gift code is a 100%-off order. A guessable one can be stumbled onto by a customer who was never given it, so they stay random by design and the naming box is never offered for them.

ⓘ Affiliate codes track, they do not pay

LOT’s affiliate codes record the revenue a creator sent us. They do not earn the creator a commission, which is why no commission figure is shown against them.

Reading it

Each row shows the code, its pool, whether it has been Used (green YES, else a dash), the order it was redeemed on, the order value, when it was used, and whether it is tied to an engagement. Filter with the All / Unused / Used tabs.

ⓘ Pre-minted, and view-only today

Codes are minted into the pool in advance, not created here; a code becomes “used” when a customer redeems it on an order, which fills in the order, value and engagement link. Bulk generation of codes is a later phase, so this screen is read-only for now. The list shows up to 200 codes.

chapters.title: Targets
chapters.html:
Targets is where you set a views goal and a spend budget for each month, then watch how the real numbers track against them. It turns the month into a simple scorecard: are we on pace for views, and are we inside budget?

What it’s for
Monthly views & budget goals.
Read or act?
Read tracking; set targets.
Who
Marketer Lead Admin
Set by
Manage access.

Setting a month

  1. Pick the month. In the top panel, choose the month you are setting a goal for.
  2. Enter the goals. Type a target views number and a budget in rupees, plus an optional note.
  3. Save. The month appears in the tracking table below, and re-saving the same month overwrites it.

Reading the tracking table

One row per month shows the target views beside the actual views achieved, and the budget beside the actual spend, each with a progress bar. The current month is marked in orange. The actuals are not typed in: they add themselves up from the live deals and payments for that month, so the table always reflects reality without anyone updating it.

What the colours mean

BarReading it
ViewsFills toward the goal and turns green once it reaches it. More is better.
SpendStays calm while there is room, shifts amber as it nears the budget and red once over. Less is better.
★ Click a row to edit it

Clicking any month in the tracking table loads its numbers back into the panel at the top, ready to adjust and save again. It is the quick way to nudge a goal without retyping the month.

ⓘ Targets are per month, for the whole team

A target covers the month as a whole, not a single influencer or product, and there is one set of numbers per month. Everyone can see the tracking; setting and changing the goals needs manage access. If you only see the table and not the set-a-month panel, your access is view-only, which is normal.

chapters.title: Reports
chapters.html:
Reports is the planned home for spend and performance analytics. Today it is a placeholder while the reports are built.

What it’s for
Spend & performance analytics.
Read or act?
Read-only (placeholder).
Who
Lead Admin
Status
Phase B (coming).

What’s coming

The screen previews the reports planned for a later phase: spend by month, ROAS by product, a CPM distribution, and top performers. Until then it shows a placeholder card rather than live charts.

ⓘ Empty is expected here

Two different messages can appear: if you lack the reports permission you see “You don’t have permission to view reports”; if you have it, you still see only the placeholder, because the reports themselves are not built yet. Both are normal today.

parts.subtitle: Where user roles are managed, and how the legacy sheet is imported.

chapters.title: User Roles
chapters.html:
User Roles explains how Ignition’s permissions work and where to manage them. Ignition does not manage accounts itself: it reuses the shared company roles, and assignment happens in Garage.

What it’s for
Explaining where roles are set.
Read or act?
Read-only (reference).
Who
Admin
Manage in
Garage → Users.

What it tells you

The page explains that Ignition uses the shared permission map, lists the five Ignition permissions (ignition_view, ignition_manage, ignition_approve, ignition_admin, ignition_reports_view), and notes the two bundled roles: ignition_manager (view, manage, reports) and ignition_lead (adds Reports). Approval is admin-only since 26 Aug 2026 — ignition_approve was moved off Lead so that final sign-off on a proposed deal rests with the Marketing head. Admins and super admins get everything automatically.

ⓘ There is no user table here

Despite the name, this screen has no “add user” controls. To actually change someone’s access, go to Garage → Users and set their role there; it then takes effect across Ignition.

chapters.title: Sheet Import
chapters.html:
Sheet Import documents how the legacy “Omnipresent” influencer spreadsheet is loaded into Ignition. It is a reference runbook for the technical team, not a button you click.

What it’s for
Documenting the data import.
Read or act?
Read-only (instructions).
Who
Admin (technical)
How
A command-line script.

What it explains

The page lays out the one-time migration steps: place the latest Omnipresent - Influencer.xlsx in Downloads, run the import script from the workspace, which posts the rows into the database through one-shot import routines. The import is idempotent (re-running it will not create duplicates), and the routines are removed afterward.

⚠ No upload button here

Despite the name, there is nothing to click on this screen: it is a runbook for an engineer doing a data migration from the command line. For day-to-day work you will never need it; influencers and engagements are added through the normal screens.
